mappings.note: Asks what the baby's smile can melt; the key is the hard-hearted person's MIND, so the item decodes the paashaan image. Rejected LO-6: not plain content recall but the rupak referent, which policy sends to kaavya-saundarya/bhaav-paksh.
taatparya of 'jhopdi mein kamal khilna' -- an image whose sense is joy inside poverty. Rejected LO-6 because nothing literal is being recalled; the bimb is being interpreted.
Plain who-question: whose smile the extract describes (baal shishu). Rejected LO-7: no saundarya, bimb or shilp is under discussion, only the poem's content.
Literal recall of the shishu's dhool-sana body. Rejected LO-7 because the item stops at the stated fact and does not ask for the upamaan or its effect.
Who is gazing unblinkingly at the poet -- narrative content. Rejected LO-7: no interpretation of kala-paksh is required.
Who introduced the child to the poet; plain kaavyabodh recall. Rejected LO-7 because no figurative expression is being unpacked.
Why the child failed to recognise the poet -- narrative cause inside the poem. Rejected LO-7: the answer is situational fact, not bhaav-paksh commentary.
What the poet would have missed without the mother as medium; content inference. Rejected LO-7 because no image or craft feature is analysed.

Asks what the dust-covered body SEEMS LIKE (kamal) -- that is the upamaan of the poem's comparison, which policy routes to kala-paksh. Rejected LO-5: the item never names or asks to identify the alankaar, only its upamaan.
Which sight prompted the paashaan-to-water imagining; the answer is the poem's own subject, plain recall. Rejected LO-7 because the item asks WHO/WHAT, not what the image means.
What the poet holds about the crop -- the stated thought of 'Fasal'. Rejected LO-7: no shilp, ras or saundarya question, just the poem's proposition.
Recall of the line 'karodon haathon ke sparsh ki garima'. Rejected LO-7 because the direction is text-recall, not interpretation of the metaphor.
How many rivers' water -- literal detail (dheron). Rejected LO-7: nothing figurative is decoded.
What the poem 'Fasal' is about; subject-matter comprehension. Rejected LO-2, which would apply only if the question were about the poem's chhand, lay or bhaasha.

Names the alankaar in 'laakh-laakh, koti-koti' (punarukti). LO-5 is the only alankaar outcome in this frame, so punarukti goes here; rejected LO-2 because repetition is being classed as an alankaar, not as tuk/lay.
What works like magic for the crops (river water) -- literal recall. Rejected LO-7: the metaphor 'jaadu' is not itself being explained here, only the referent named in the poem.
Through whom the poet saw the smile; plain content. Rejected LO-7 because no bhaav or kala-paksh analysis is asked.
How the smile strikes the poet (mohak) -- a stated reaction. Rejected LO-7: the item takes a one-word content answer, not a manahsthiti description.
What contributes to the crop growing -- content list. Rejected LO-7 because nothing figurative or craft-related is probed.

Explicit 'se kya abhipraay' on 'koti-koti haathon ke sparsh ki garima' -- interpretation of the image. Rejected LO-6: the sibling would fit only the recall form of this line (item 12), not its abhipraay.

Why the line 'ek ke nahin, do ke nahin' is repeated -- the effect of a shilp device (saamoohikta ka bhaav). Rejected LO-5 because the stem does not name or ask to identify punarukti; it asks the purpose, which is kala-paksh.
Subject-matter of 'Fasal' (the factors needed for crop production). Rejected LO-7: theme recall, not saundarya or shilp.
Recall of whose transformed form the crop is (the sun's rays), straight from the line. Rejected LO-7 because the item does not ask what that transformation signifies.
What the crop is per the poet -- fruit of labour and of nature, the poem's stated position. Rejected LO-7: no interpretive or aesthetic demand.
Asks the 'nihit bhaav' of the line 'haathon ke sparsh ki mahima' -- bhaav-paksh explicitly. Rejected LO-6 because the item names bhaav, not content.
Why the infant stares (wants to recognise the poet) -- narrative reason. Rejected LO-7: no image is decoded.
taatparya of 'murde mein bhi jaan daal deti hai' -- an atishayokti whose sense is hope returning to the despairing. Rejected LO-6 because the literal reading is explicitly the wrong option.
What the poet calls himself (chir pravaasi, atithi) -- the poem's own words recalled. Rejected LO-7: the epithet's own wording is the answer, not its significance.
With whom the child has had no contact (the poet himself); situational content. Rejected LO-7 because nothing aesthetic is analysed.
Whose eyes met -- literal content. Rejected LO-7: 'aankhen chaar hona' is glossed by the poem's own situation, not treated as a bimb to interpret.
Whose fingers fed the child madhuparka; plain recall. Rejected LO-7 because the madhuparka image is not itself the question.
Which epithets the poet uses for himself -- recall of the poem's words. Rejected LO-7, which would fit 'why' he uses them (see item 109), not 'which'.
Who the child's first teacher is -- the poem's thematic content about the mother as medium. Rejected C-H1.3 because this is not literary history but a kaavyabodh answer.
What seems chhavimaan to the poet (the child's smile) -- content recall. Rejected LO-7 because the item stops at naming the referent of the poem's adjective.
taatparya of 'paashaan pighalna' -- pity born in a hard heart, a rupak being unpacked. Rejected LO-6 since the literal stone-melting option is the distractor.
Why the child could not recognise the poet -- narrative cause. Rejected LO-7: no interpretation of imagery. (Near-duplicate of item 7.)
What the poem says can revive a dead man (the child's smile) -- naming the referent as stated. Rejected LO-7, which fits the 'what does that mean' form of the same line (items 27, 117).
What the poet calls himself (chir-pravaasi); recall of the poem's wording. Rejected LO-7 because no significance is demanded.
What falls from the babool at the child's touch (shefaalika flowers) -- literal detail. Rejected LO-7: the item asks the fact, not the meaning of the transformation.
Whom besides the infant the poet calls blessed (the mother) -- content recall. Rejected LO-7, which would fit the 'why is she blessed' form (item 106).
Gloss of the poem's own coinage 'danturit'. Rejected C-H1.2 because this is not a decontextualised grammar/vocabulary item; the word is the poem's title word.
Gloss of the poem's word 'animesh'. Rejected C-H1.2: the word carries poem content, so it belongs with kaavyabodh, not with vyaakaran.
Gloss of the poem's word 'kankhi'. Rejected C-H1.2 for the same reason -- it is the poem's diction, not a standalone shabd-bhandaar drill.
What the poem depicts (the child's smile) -- subject-matter. Rejected C-H1.3 because nothing about the poet or literary history is asked.
Asks which alankaar is in the quoted couplet (atishayokti). Rejected LO-7: the demand is alankaar identification, which is exactly LO-5, not a general kala-paksh explanation.
Who the infant's first teacher is -- thematic content of the poem. Rejected C-H1.3 as no literary-history knowledge is involved. (Duplicate of item 33.)
Asks who wrote 'Yah Danturit Muskaan' -- authorship/literary history, and this frame has no biography LO. Rejected LO-6 because the answer is not in the poem's content at all.
Whose smile is called danturit (the child's) -- content recall. Rejected LO-7 because 'danturit muskaan' is glossed literally here, not treated as a bimb.
Into whom the smile puts life (mritak) -- the poem's stated claim. Rejected LO-7, reserved for the 'how/what does it mean' form of this line (items 27, 124).
Gloss of 'jaljaat' (kamal), a word from the poem. Rejected C-H1.2 because the word is poem diction rather than a general paryaayvaachi exercise.
What was blooming in the poet's hut (jaljaat) -- literal recall. Rejected LO-7, which fits the 'what does the blooming lotus mean' form (items 2, 113).
Whose touch melted the stone (the child's) -- naming the agent as the poem states. Rejected LO-7 because the image's sense is not asked.
What made the shefaalika flowers fall -- literal content. Rejected LO-7: fact, not interpretation.
Gloss of 'animesh dekhna' from the poem. Rejected C-H1.2 because the phrase is the poem's own, not a detached muhaavara item.
Who is the medium of the introduction (the mother) -- plain content. Rejected LO-7 as no aesthetic feature is analysed.
Whom the poet calls chir pravaasi (himself). 'Chir pravaasi' is a literal self-description, not a prateek, so rejected LO-7 despite the 'kise kaha hai' phrasing.
Whose fingers fed the child madhuparka -- literal recall. Rejected LO-7 because the madhuparka image itself is not the question. (Duplicate of item 31.)
Asks the EFFECT of the danturit smile on the poet -- his bhaav and manahsthiti. Rejected LO-6 because the answer is the poem's emotional impact, not a retrievable fact.
Whom the infant fails to recognise (the poet) -- narrative content. Rejected LO-7 as nothing figurative is unpacked.
aashay of 'pighal kar jal ban gaya hoga kathin paashaan', keyed to the poet's own hard heart softening -- rupak decoding. Rejected LO-6 because the literal stone reading is the distractor.
